living.note: 3-seat settee 850 deep + body 300 + armchair 850 deep = 2000 across; settee 1850 long

dining.note: 4-person table 1000 x 1200 (Neufert 600 x 400 per place + 200 serving strip) + body 300 on the served side of each axis

kitchen.note: base-unit run 600 deep + body 300 across the aisle; Neufert's work sequence store-wash-prepare-cook = fridge 600 + sink/drainer 900 + hob 600 along the run

bedroom_principal.note: principal double 1500 x 2000 + body 300 to BOTH sides and the foot (AD M M4(2) 2.25 gives the principal double both sides)

bedroom_double.note: double bed 1350 x 1900 + body 300 to one side (AD M M4(2) 2.25)

bedroom_single.note: single bed 900 x 1900 + body 300 to one side (AD M M4(2) 2.25)

study.note: desk 500 x 1050 (AD M Appendix D 'table and chair') + body 300

bathroom.note: bath 700 deep + body 300 alongside; bath 1700 long. Pan and basin occupy the same strip as the body zone, which is shared

shower_room.note: tray 900 beside pan 500 = 1400 along the wall; across, the deeper of the 900 tray and pan 700 + body 300

wc.note: pan and cistern 500 x 700 + body 300 to one side and in front

utility.note: unit run 600 deep + body 300; sink/drainer 900 + washing machine 600

hall.note: AD M M4(2) 2.22a clear width 900; entrance leaf 838 + body 300 for the swing

entrance_lobby.note: as hall; the two differ in programme, not in geometry

corridor.note: AD M M4(2) 2.22a clear width 900, both axes. A corridor has no second dimension of its own

storage.note: shelf depth 600; shelf 600 + body 300 to reach it

living_dining.note: permissive envelope over the packings of living + dining: 1850 x 3300; 2000 x 3150

kitchen_dining.note: permissive envelope over the packings of kitchen + dining: 1300 x 3600; 1500 x 3400; 2100 x 2200

living_dining_kitchen.note: permissive envelope over the packings of living + dining + kitchen: 1850 x 5400; 2000 x 5250; 2100 x 4050
